text.p: Colombia coach Hernan Dario Gomez contemplated resigning on Thursday after seeing his team lose their third successive World Cup qualifying match.

His team's apparently smooth progress to next year's World Cup in France has hit turbulence after Wednesday's shock 1-0 defeat at home to Peru which came in the wake of earlier losses at home to Argentina and away to Paraguay.

"I don't want to leave the team but if that is the best thing for our qualification hopes then I will not hesistate to do it," he told a news conference in the Caribbean port city. "At the moment, the situation is worrying."

Gomez, who has received the backing of the Colombian Football Federation, also admitted he was considering rebuilding the team completely, and would use next month's Copa America to field younger players.

Colombia's team has changed little over the last decade, with players such as Carlos Valderrama, Freddy Rincon and Leonel Alvarez becoming almost permanent fixtures. Gomez himself was assistant to former coach Francisco Maturana before taking over in 1994.
He discarded the option of playing Colombia's remaining home games at other venues after his team were jeered off the field.
Colombia have made Barranquilla their home for the last ten years, preferring the steamy conditions to the altitude of the capital Bogota.
Colombia were unbeaten in their first seven qualifying games and appeared destined to win the nine-team group easily.

They now find themselves six points behind leaders Paraguay, one ahead of third-placed Argentina and only four in front of the chasing pack of Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Uruguay. Four teams qualify for France.
